text:
marina: Observing a sudden latency spike across na1 hotpool since 08:14 UTC, requests piling on GPU nodes. Not a regional network issue (edges look OK).

sanjeev: Confirmed. P95 tokens generation latency jumped from 120ms -> 850ms. Errorrate + KV cache miss rate both up.

olivia: Any recent rollouts to runtime or batching?

marina: Runtime +continuous-batcher v2 rollout at 08:05 (canary -> 50%). Change introduced new packer that groups by token-length heuristics.

dave: I see increased KV eviction churn in the logs: 
```
kvcache: eviction_rate=0.34 event=compaction reason=collision
batcher: added_window_size=512 -> 1024
```
Seems like packer is creating larger batches that cause per-request memory pressure and more KV miss thrashing.

paul: deploy-bot: rollout continuous-batcher:v2 -> canary 50% at 08:05 UTC

oncall-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-342 - na1 hotpool latency spike

sanjeev: I'd recommend immediate canary rollback to v1 on hotpool nodes, and shift traffic off na1 hotpool to na2 for high-priority routes. Rolling rollback now?

marina: Rolling back canary on hotpool now: `kubectl set image daemonset/continuous-batcher continuous-batcher=continuous-batcher:v1 -n runtime`

olivia: While rollback runs, can we temporarily reduce batching window size via runtime flag to avoid OOMs? Param is `--max-batch-tokens=512` (default 1024 on v2).

marina: Applied `--max-batch-tokens=512` on hotpool nodes via ssm param set and restarted pods.

paul: Observability: KV cache miss rate dropped from 72% -> 48% after flag change, but p95 still high (520ms).

dave: Looks like hotpool GPU utilization is saturated and there's queuing. Autoscaler isn't adding nodes because GPU quota in na1 is exhausted. We need immediate traffic spill to na2/na3.

olivia: Initiating traffic diversion: `routesctl shift --from=na1-hotpool --to=na2-hotpool --percent=40 --reason=latency-spike`

marina: Doing gradual shift: +10% every 2min. Noted some customers with strict data residency — we must whitelist excluded routes.

paul: Also enabling CPU-fallback for low-priority orgs to keep latency bounded for critical users. This will increase cost. Approve?

sanjeev: Approve for low-priority orgs <-> cost center temporary. Add annotation so finance knows.

marina: CPU-fallback enabled for tag:nonpaying. Annotated incident with cost estimate: ~$4k/day extra while active.

deploy-bot: rollback continuous-batcher:v2 -> v1 succeeded on 12/6 hotpool nodes at 08:28 UTC

paul: After rollback + traffic shift, p95 is back to ~150ms on na2 and 240ms on na1. KV eviction settled.

dave: For postmortem: we need a preflight test for batcher memory footprint for mixed-length workloads and quota-aware routing when autoscaler hits NVIDIA quota. Add a guard to prevent packer widening beyond node memory threshold.

olivia: Agreed. Action items: 1) add memory guard in packer (olivia) 2) add autoscaler quota check + spill policy (dave) 3) add canary traffic cap for packer changes (marina) 4) finance notif for CPU-fallback (paul).

marina: I'll schedule a hotpool repro run with long-tail prompts to validate guard. Also we should add a dashboard for "batcher effective batch size" and kvcache eviction delta.

sanjeev: Closing incident once we confirm stable for 30m. Current plan: keep 40% shifted for 10m then drop back.

paul: FYI — cost impact estimate updated: $2.8k for the 4h mitigation window (reduced from initial estimate). Logged to incident ticket.

oncall-bot: incident #INC-2026-342 status: mitigated -> monitoring (08:55 UTC)

marina: Monitoring looks green at 09:02 UTC. Will follow up with postmortem doc in /docs/incidents/na1-hotpool-batcher-2026.md. Thanks all.
